subject: Stability saddle and procurement lifecycle note: MAP refresh + bridging options
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <ogrant@medisa.com>, Medisa Procurement <procurement@medisa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Stability saddle and procurement lifecycle note: MAP refresh + bridging options

Oliver / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Medisa's acceptance window has tightened and the original MAP milestones no longer align with your procurement gating. I attached an updated MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) that compresses the evaluation phase by one week and introduces two contingency lanes: a procurement-friendly "bridging" cadence and a fall-through credit plan. High-level summary below: 

- Compressed evaluation: reduce staged perf tests from 6 -> 4 business days by running parallel canaries (week of Nov 22).
- Procurement bridging: temporary invoicing hold + phased DocuSign sign-off per module to allow pilot traffic to run while legal finishes exhibit redlines.
- Credit plan: limited one-time credit (see credit_plan_summary.pdf) tied to acceptance lag beyond 3 business days.

Open asks: 
1) Can procurement confirm whether phased signature by module is workable (legal ok with partial exhibits)?
2) Procurement to share an ETA for the redline review (procurement_redlines_medisa.pdf attached contains our suggested edits).
3) Oliver — confirm a firm date you can commit for the pilot kick (Nov 30 or earlier?)

If you prefer, we can run a 30-minute legal + procurement bridge session on Friday to align exhibits and finalize the DocuSign envelope. I added Marissa and Ben as they're leading the MAP changes and credit evaluation.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Oliver Grant <ogrant@medisa.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Medisa Procurement <procurement@medisa.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stability saddle and procurement lifecycle note: MAP refresh + bridging options

Thanks, Jasmine — appreciate the proactive layout. A few quick points from our side: 

- Procurement is open to phased signatures in principle, but legal will need to see the exact exhibit language before we can commit to partial sign-off.
- Our legal team will aim to return redlines by EOD Tue (Nov 16). If there are material changes, that might push the pilot to the week of Nov 29.
- Regarding credits: the team is sensitive to precedent. Can you confirm the maximum credit you can authorize at AE level before needing finance sign-off?

If you can host the bridge session on Friday at 11am PT, I'll get our procurement counsel on the invite.

—Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Partnerships, Medisa Health
ogrant@medisa.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <ogrant@medisa.com>, Medisa Procurement <procurement@medisa.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stability saddle and procurement lifecycle note: MAP refresh + bridging options

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 10:05 AM Oliver Grant <ogrant@medisa.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Jasmine — appreciate the proactive layout. A few quick points from our side: 
> 
> - Procurement is open to phased signatures in principle, but legal will need to see the exact exhibit language before we can commit to partial sign-off.
> - Our legal team will aim to return redlines by EOD Tue (Nov 16). If there are material changes, that might push the pilot to the week of Nov 29.
> - Regarding credits: the team is sensitive to precedent. Can you confirm the maximum credit you can authorize at AE level before needing finance sign-off?

Thanks for the quick read, Oliver. To be explicit on the credit question: as AE I can approve up to a 10% one-time activation credit tied to late acceptance; anything above that requires approval from finance and my manager. I've included a conservative credit-tier in credit_plan_summary.pdf — it is structured so finance review is only needed if we hit the highest tier.

Operational mitigation I recommend if redlines slip: (1) run the pilot under a limited data sandbox (no PHI) to start on Nov 29, (2) stash acceptance gating behind our feature flags so Medisa can opt into production traffic once exhibits are finalized. Both reduce risk to your compliance team while keeping the momentum.

If procurement's redlines arrive on schedule we can lock Nov 29 as pilot start; if not, I propose Nov 30 as soft fallback with a firm re-eval on Nov 18 (see below).

-M
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachment: credit_plan_summary.pdf (brief)

From: Medisa Procurement <procurement@medisa.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <ogrant@medisa.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stability saddle and procurement lifecycle note: MAP refresh + bridging options

Hi Marissa / Jasmine —

Please find our redlines attached (procurement_redlines_medisa.pdf). Key asks from legal: 
- Clarify data residency and logging retention for pilot traffic (we need a 30-day sandbox retention pledge).
- Exhibit B (SLAs) — request removal of the 24-hour support response commitment for pilot phase; legal prefers an M-F 8am–6pm SLA during evaluation.
- Add a clause for a trial termination window (7 days) if the pilot reveals unaddressed compliance gaps.

We can make progress on phased signature if Redwood can accept the sandbox retention and the pilot SLA modifications. We'll aim to have a clean DocuSign envelope by Tue Nov 17 EOD if we can resolve these three points today. I've also dropped a DocuSign link for the current packet: https://docusign.com/embedded/abc123

Thanks,
Medisa Procurement
Attachment: procurement_redlines_medisa.pdf (redlines)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Medisa Procurement <procurement@medisa.com>, Oliver Grant <ogrant@medisa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stability saddle and procurement lifecycle note: MAP refresh + bridging options — Nov 18 update and decision lane

Team — quick status and recommended path forward after internal huddle this morning: 

Status summary: 
- Procurement redlines received (thanks) — we can accept sandbox retention at 30 days for the pilot and adjust Exhibit B SLA to M-F 8–6 for evaluation only.
- DocuSign envelope updated; legal asked for a single signature lane with an exhibit checklist to enable module-level activation once exhibits clear.
- Oliver: based on the above, we can commit to a pilot kick on Nov 29 under sandbox conditions. If Medisa confirms the envelope by Tue Nov 23 EOD we will commit engineering readiness and can run parallel canaries that week.

Risk ladder and triggers (for Medisa and Redwood alignment): 
- Low risk: redlines signed by Nov 23 -> pilot start Nov 29, full acceptance window unchanged.
- Medium risk: redlines sign by Nov 26 -> pilot start Dec 2, apply 5% activation credit (automatic).
- High risk: redlines sign after Nov 26 or not signed -> postpone pilot and trigger exec sync; potential 10% credit requires finance approval.

Next steps / requests: 
1) Medisa to confirm DocuSign by Nov 23 EOD (procurement).
2) Medisa to confirm whether the sandbox retention 30-day pledge is acceptable (legal).
3) Redwood to run Friday bridge session if any outstanding legal bullets remain — recommended if redlines come back with follow-ups.

I've attached the final MAP_v2.xlsx and the credit_plan_summary.pdf for your records. I'll loop in Laura from Finance for approvals if we hit the medium/high triggers.

Thanks and looking forward to locking dates,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx, credit_plan_summary.pdf
